neighbours.label: Repeating an object or action in coordinated alternatives that lead to contrasting outcomes.
fire: You can carry the suitcase and tire your arms or leave the suitcase and lose your supplies.
She could open the window and hear the traffic or close the window and miss the breeze.
We can repair the fence and spend our savings or ignore the fence and risk another escape.
He could take the shortcut and arrive early or avoid the shortcut and stay on the marked trail.
They can heat the room and use more fuel or leave the room unheated and wear heavier coats.
I could accept the offer and move away or reject the offer and remain near my family.
The team can run the test and delay the release or skip the test and risk an unseen defect.
You could keep the receipt and request a refund or discard the receipt and lose that option.
quiet: Carrying the suitcase may tire your arms, while leaving it behind would mean losing your supplies.
Opening the window brings traffic noise; closing it instead prevents the breeze from entering.
Repairing the fence would consume our savings, whereas ignoring it risks another escape.
Taking the shortcut might save time; avoiding it would keep him on the marked trail.
Heating the room uses additional fuel, while warmer coats make the cold more tolerable.
Accepting the offer requires moving away; refusing it allows me to remain near my family.
Running the test delays release, whereas skipping it leaves a risk of an unseen defect.
Keeping the receipt makes a refund possible; throwing it away removes that option.

notes: Simple noun lists and ordinary coordination were weak in exploration. A repeated object followed by contrasting coordinated outcomes was stronger, motivating this narrower hypothesis. Controls retain both alternatives and their consequences while removing repeated full noun phrases. The broad card contains many unrelated code and list-ending peaks.
